title: Pog and the Whispering Woods
markdown:
In the craggy highlands of Misty Kettle, where the wind whispered secrets and the rocks wore mossy coats, lived a little goblin named Pog. Knobbly knees peeked from his tunic. His grin was as wide as a summer sky. He loved his cozy hollow under a mossy rock. He was not, however, very organised. Not one bit.

One bright morning a letter fluttered down, delivered by a remarkably speedy bee. Elara, his elf pen-friend, was coming next week. She could hardly wait to see his mountain home. Would they have the special Moonpetal Mushroom tea he had told her about?

Pog’s heart jigged. He must appear clever. He grabbed his trusty twig—his wand of purpose—and his worn Goblin’s Guide to Essential Errands, Chapter One: Foraging for Fungi. Look near twisty trees and bubbling brooks. Simple enough.

The Whispering Woods welcomed him with dappled sun, damp earth, and the murmur of unseen creatures. He hummed, picturing Elara’s smile. But the woods were twistier than imagined. One tree mirrored another. The brook curved back on itself as if playing chase. A rustle in the undergrowth made his knees knock like tiny castanets. The book had not mentioned this.

A deep rumbling sound vibrated the air. Pog froze, scrambled behind a giant speckled toadstool, and pulled its wide cap down. Then: a soft contented sigh, and gentle humming. He peeked.

In a patch of sunlight stood Tansy, a truly enormous ogre, shoulders broad as boulders, large leathery hands patting soil around plants that glowed with soft silvery light. Not a roar. A low resonant tune. Night-blooms. Curiosity fizzed. Tansy did not look fearsome. Tansy looked rather gentle.

Pog stepped out. “Excuse me?” A squeak. Tansy turned, kind eyes widening. “Well now, what have we here? Lost, little one? Or admiring the Moonpetals?”

“A bit. I’m Pog. I’m looking for Moonpetal Mushrooms for tea. My friend Elara is coming to visit. My book says they grow near here, but these trees are a bit tangled.”

Tansy chuckled, distant thunder. “They do love damp cool spots. You’re in luck. I just picked some.” From a sturdy woven basket: mushrooms shimmering like captured moonbeams. “Don’t you worry about being lost. The woods can play tricks. Often the very best thing is simply to ask for help. These trees get rather overexcited about growing.”

Pog took them carefully, scent sweet and earthy. “Thank you. You’re not a fearsome beast at all.”

Tansy winked. “Only to weeds, sometimes.”

The sky painted itself purple and rose. Pog scampered home, mushrooms in his satchel. He had not been perfectly organised. He had asked. He had found tea, and a friend.

And so Pog learned that being clever is not knowing everything beforehand, but being willing to ask, even when the trees are tangled.
